Independent interface review · 17 October 2026

Platform UX & accessibility audit

A screen-by-screen review of the running Omnichannel Orchestration Reference platform in Chrome. Spacing, alignment, colors, forms, ARIA and keyboard consistency — with captured evidence and actionable corrections.

28 findings4 P118 P26 P375 captured states

Markdown findings and coverage · Findings JSON · Keyboard evidence

Coverage and limits. All main navigation sections and Settings subsections; representative details, dialogs, email/Push editing, send planning and archived messages. Desktop plus tablet/phone samples. Empty approvals prevent request-detail review; authenticated sign-in redirects prevented login review. Dark mode, live screen-reader audio, AI results, recovery/error states and every module variation remain untested. No saved edits, sends, approvals or permission changes. This is an audit, not a conformance certificate or an implementation commitment.

The strongest problems are component-layout regressions. The core palette is coherent, and sampled list, Escape, menu-arrow and focus-return behavior works. Screenshot outlines identify relevant areas; ARIA and interaction findings also require the accompanying reproduction notes.

P1 UX-01 · Defect · Image picker / Library

Image thumbnails overflow their buttons and overlap the filters

Each image button measures 28 px high while its image measures 96 px high. The images overlap adjacent rows and extend into the filter area; names and sizes are visually obscured. Reproduced at desktop and phone widths.

Why it matters It is difficult to identify an asset or know which image a click will select.

Suggested correction Give image cards intrinsic height, prevent flex shrinking of thumbnails, and reserve separate rows for thumbnail, name and dimensions. Keep the grid below the filters.

Reproduction and source

Open an email or Push variant → Change image… → Library.

frontend/src/index.css:155; frontend/src/index.css:1242

P1 UX-02 · Defect · Create dialogs

New record and New audience use a broken horizontal form layout

The heading and first field share a row; fields are only about 164 px wide. Help text wraps beside fields. New category, New campaign and Settings creation dialogs instead use a full-width vertical form.

Why it matters The first input looks attached to the title; labels, fields and actions lack a reliable reading order visually.

Suggested correction Use the same vertical dialog form and footer component as New category. Keep the heading outside the field layout.

Reproduction and source

Records → New record; compare Audiences → New audience and Categories → New category.

frontend/src/screens/ContentCreate.tsx:51; frontend/src/screens/AudienceCreate.tsx:54; frontend/src/index.css:758

P1 UX-03 · Defect · Content / Graph

Category graph labels collide with nodes and edges

Multiple labels sit under adjacent circles or cross the dense edge bundle. Several category names are partially obscured.

Why it matters The drawing does not reliably communicate category names or relationships. The accessible table helps but does not repair the visual graph.

Suggested correction Separate labels from node geometry, reduce edge density until a category is selected, and add zoom or a focused neighborhood view.

Reproduction and source

Content → Graph, with the current 26-category dataset.

Live screenshot and DOM inspection

P1 UX-04 · Accessibility · Global keyboard shortcuts

Character-only shortcuts cannot be disabled or remapped

?, /, p and g-then-letter sequences are active outside text fields. The help dialog offers no off/remap control; the registry explicitly describes shortcuts as not configurable.

Why it matters Accidental activation from speech input or stray keys. This conflicts with WCAG 2.1.4 for global character-only shortcuts.

Suggested correction Provide a persistent off switch or remapping with a non-character modifier; preserve focused-widget keyboard behavior.

Reproduction and source

Focus a non-input control → ?; review the help. Test g then c and / outside text inputs.

frontend/src/shortcuts/Shortcuts.tsx:76

P2 UX-05 · Defect · Keyboard shortcuts dialog

Global navigation shortcuts operate behind an open modal

Opened shortcut help on Settings → Brands. With Close focused, g then c changed the URL and background to Campaigns while the dialog stayed open.

Why it matters The modal does not isolate navigation commands; its content can change beneath the user.

Suggested correction Suspend background commands while a modal is open, or make modal navigation an explicit action that closes the dialog and intentionally restores focus.

Reproduction and source

Settings → Brands → ? → focus Close → g then c.

frontend/src/shortcuts/Shortcuts.tsx:76

P2 UX-06 · Accessibility · Record fields / profile multiline fields

Textarea borders use the weak divider color

Body text (long) has a 1 px #e4daca border on white, about 1.38:1 contrast. Single-line fields use the stronger #857a6c border, about 4.20:1. The textarea background is also white, so the boundary is its principal visible affordance.

Why it matters Multiline editable areas are harder to distinguish, especially with low vision; review against WCAG 1.4.11.

Suggested correction Use the strong field-border token for textareas as for inputs. Keep decorative card separators on the weaker token.

Reproduction and source

Open a record → scroll to Body text (long); compare the surrounding inputs.

frontend/src/index.css:765

P2 UX-07 · Defect · Personalise menu

Personalisation labels run into token names

The menu renders “Salutation formal{{salutation_formal}}” with no visual gap. The same happens on phone width.

Why it matters Labels and machine tokens cannot be scanned independently.

Suggested correction Use a two-column menu row with a real gap; style the token in monospace and allow truncation or wrapping without colliding.

Reproduction and source

In a variant field → Personalise….

frontend/src/components/EditorFields.tsx:177

P2 UX-08 · Accessibility · Record and variant editors

Repeated Personalise buttons have identical accessible names

Every field action is named “Personalise…”. The sampled controls have no field-specific aria-label or aria-describedby association.

Why it matters A screen-reader button list does not reveal which field each action edits.

Suggested correction Name actions by field, e.g. “Personalise subject line” and “Personalise headline”, while retaining concise visible text.

Reproduction and source

Inspect the editor accessibility tree or navigate among its Personalise buttons.

frontend/src/components/EditorFields.tsx:173

P2 UX-09 · Accessibility · Settings / Users / Access

Role-removal buttons do not name the role or brand

The two access rows each expose a button named only “Remove”, for Admin on two different brands. Other parts of the platform use names such as “Remove Biwak”.

Why it matters The consequence of the action is ambiguous when navigating controls by name.

Suggested correction Use “Remove Admin on Grathaus Outdoor” and the equivalent name for each assignment.

Reproduction and source

Settings → Users → Initial admin → inspect Access.

P2 UX-10 · Accessibility · Recipients / detail

Recipient data tables have no column or row headers

Consent renders channel, purpose, status, source and time as td-only rows. Interests and Consent history follow the same pattern.

Why it matters Relationships between values are not programmatically identified; “demo” and a timestamp have no announced header context.

Suggested correction Add visible column headings with th/scope, a row header where appropriate, and a concise table caption or accessible label.

Reproduction and source

Recipients → grathaus-1000 → inspect Consent and lower tables.

frontend/src/screens/RecipientDetail.tsx:42

P2 UX-11 · Defect · Settings / General

General settings facts lose the card content inset

In Sending and AI, label/value rows start at the left card edge while neighboring inputs and buttons start 16 px inside. The AI facts appear as ungrouped lines rather than the fact rows used elsewhere.

Why it matters The vertical alignment breaks within the same card and weakens label/value grouping.

Suggested correction Render these facts with the shared fact-row component and the same 16 px content inset.

Reproduction and source

Settings → General → compare Sending; scroll to AI.

P2 UX-12 · Defect · Category, record and access forms

Inline action buttons align with labels instead of inputs

The Add button in “Put it under” is level with the label, above the selection field. Duplicate on records, Give in user access, and Issue a key show the same staggered baseline.

Why it matters Connected controls look unrelated and the horizontal alignment feels unfinished.

Suggested correction Align the button with the input/control bottom edge, accounting for field label height and bottom margins.

Reproduction and source

Categories → Wandern → Put it under. Compare record Duplicate and user Give a role.

P3 UX-13 · Inconsistency · Modals across the app

Dialog headers and action order vary

The image picker puts Close below its heading on the left. Preview puts Close in a right-aligned header. Paste people stacks Check and Cancel; the broken creation forms place Create before Cancel, while the standard dialogs put Cancel before Create at the right.

Why it matters Users must relearn where to dismiss or confirm each dialog.

Suggested correction Adopt shared modal-header and action-footer patterns; use a consistent Cancel → primary-action order.

Reproduction and source

Compare Change image…, Open preview, New record, New category and Paste people.

Live screenshot and DOM inspection

P2 UX-14 · Recommendation · Settings / Brand profile

Long profile form has its only Save action at the bottom

Save is a normal card near the end of a multi-screen form and scrolls away. There is no persistent save action while editing the earlier sections.

Why it matters Saving requires a long scroll and the commitment model is easy to miss.

Suggested correction Keep a compact Save/dirty-state action area visible while editing, or provide deliberate section-level saves.

Reproduction and source

Open Newsletter Deutsch and scroll through Legal details, Look, Header and Footer.

Live screenshot and DOM inspection

P2 UX-15 · Recommendation · Records versus brand profiles and expressions

Autosave and explicit-save screens do not explain their difference

Records use blur-based AutosaveField; profile forms have Save; expression Save is enabled even before any edit. At rest, the record screen has no nearby explanation of its blur-save behavior. This is a clarity finding, not a claim that saves fail.

Why it matters A user can expect Save on an autosaving page or assume a profile edit already persisted.

Suggested correction Show a consistent “Saves when you leave a field” cue or saved/unsaved status, and use predictable dirty-state actions on explicit-save forms.

Reproduction and source

Compare a record detail with Newsletter Deutsch and Salutation formal; no data edit was submitted.

frontend/src/components/EditorFields.tsx:82; frontend/src/screens/Personalisation.tsx:273

P2 UX-16 · Inconsistency · Lists, menus and dialogs

ARIA system messages use German inside an English interface

The document declares lang=en and app text is English, but row selection live logs say “ausgewählt” and React Aria dismissal controls are named “Schließen”. Native file-upload controls also follow the German browser locale.

Why it matters The assistive experience switches language unexpectedly. Native browser wording and app-controlled ARIA localization need to be distinguished.

Suggested correction Set an explicit application locale for React Aria matching the chosen UI language; keep record-content languages intact.

Reproduction and source

Inspect live logs after Enter on a row and the hidden dismissal buttons in modal/menu snapshots.

Live screenshot and DOM inspection

P2 UX-17 · Recommendation · Global navigation and editor actions

Shortcuts lack a visible entry point and control metadata

Help is opened with ?, and hints appear while Alt/Ctrl is held. No visible “Keyboard shortcuts” help control was found in the shell. Sampled navigation and preview controls expose no aria-keyshortcuts.

Why it matters The shortcut system is useful once known but difficult to discover and inspect through assistive tools.

Suggested correction Add a visible, keyboard-reachable shortcuts help action. Expose supported single-key shortcuts through aria-keyshortcuts where valid, and explain sequences in help/description text.

Reproduction and source

Inspect the navigation rail and help; examine Open preview and navigation control attributes.

frontend/src/shortcuts/Shortcuts.tsx:174

P2 UX-18 · Recommendation · Send / Plan the send

Scheduled send time has no visible timezone

Choosing “At a time” reveals Send at with a local date/time value, but no timezone beside it or in the section help.

Why it matters A manager cannot confirm how the selected time will be interpreted.

Suggested correction Display the actual scheduling timezone and repeat the resolved date, time and zone before commitment.

Reproduction and source

Send Deutsch → When → At a time. Do not press Plan the send.

P2 UX-19 · Recommendation · Campaigns versus Monitoring

Campaign status and delivery status use conflicting-looking labels

Campaigns shows Familienherbst, Hüttensaison-Finale and others as “draft”; Monitoring shows those same campaigns as “Sent”. These can represent distinct states, but the campaign list does not explain that distinction.

Why it matters The same campaign appears unfinished in one section and sent in another.

Suggested correction Label the states explicitly, e.g. editing status versus latest delivery outcome, or show both. Confirm intended semantics before changing backend status logic.

Reproduction and source

Compare Campaigns and Monitoring for Familienherbst.

Live screenshot and DOM inspection

P2 UX-20 · Recommendation · Decision slots, archived messages and record help

Manager-facing content exposes internal identifiers and excessive precision

Decision explanations contain category_ids, recipient_top_score and long floating-point formulas. Other screens expose content_recommendation, list_unsubscribe, opted_in, headline_medium and an ADR number in field help.

Why it matters Routine users have to translate implementation terms to understand the result.

Suggested correction Lead with human-readable strategy, category and status labels; round displayed scores; retain exact machine data in an optional technical-details disclosure.

Reproduction and source

Decision slots → Familienherbst slot → scroll to Reasons given; compare record field help.

Live screenshot and DOM inspection

P2 UX-21 · Recommendation · Push / Preview

Push preview displays raw fields instead of a notification

The main preview shows push_title, push_body, push_image_url and push_link as a definition list. The image is a URL rather than a visible notification image.

Why it matters Managers cannot assess notification hierarchy, image composition or likely truncation.

Suggested correction Provide a clearly labelled representative notification preview, with the raw payload available as secondary details. Do not imply exact rendering across every device.

Reproduction and source

Open Testtag im Laden (Push) → Edit Push → Open preview.

P3 UX-22 · Inconsistency · Campaigns, Records and Approvals

Search and filters do not share the list title indent

Titles and row text begin at x=252 while search/filter boundaries begin at x=240. Decision history similarly offsets the filters 12 px left of its title and table text.

Why it matters The left edge zigzags, despite the handoff’s one-indent-per-column rule.

Suggested correction Choose a consistent content alignment for list headers, search and filters; distinguish control borders from text padding deliberately.

Compare Records heading, search and filters; then Decision history.

Audience header places New on a separate row

New audience and Suggest from campaign sit below the heading; Campaigns and Records place the primary New action beside the heading.

Why it matters Header height and the search position vary between otherwise equivalent list screens.

P3 UX-24 · Inconsistency · Image picker / Upload new

Upload control falls back to a different visual system

The raw file input shows the browser’s square “Datei auswählen” control next to styled English form fields.

Why it matters Upload feels like a different product surface, especially next to the segmented tabs.

Suggested correction Use a styled accessible file-picker trigger while retaining the native chooser, selected filename and supported-file help. Browser-native chooser language can remain browser-controlled.

P3 UX-25 · Recommendation · Settings / Brands

Brand rename fields are unnecessarily narrow

Brand-name inputs remain around 164 px wide in a card with ample unused space; Rename and Delete sit above the field baseline. Other detail editors stretch ordinary text fields.

Why it matters Long names require horizontal text scrolling while most of the card remains empty.

Suggested correction Use a consistent responsive form row with a flexible name field and aligned actions.

P2 UX-26 · Recommendation · Responsive editor at 390 × 844

Phone layout stacks navigation, module list and detail rather than presenting one work area

At phone width, global navigation uses about 129 px, then the module list, then the editor starts around y=366. The handoff calls for one column at a time at phone width.

Why it matters Editing begins well below the top and switching modules requires scrolling past other work areas.

Suggested correction Provide an explicit list/detail transition or compact module picker at phone width, preserving a clear Back control. Treat this as responsive design follow-up, not desktop breakage.

Reproduction and source

Set a 390 × 844 viewport and open the Push variant.

Live screenshot and DOM inspection

P2 UX-27 · Recommendation · Content / Records

Record catalogue mixes languages without showing language

English translations and German originals are interleaved. Rows expose title, description and active status but no language badge; current filters contain Status, Category and Ready for only.

Why it matters It is harder to distinguish an original from a translation or choose the right language for a channel.

Suggested correction Add a concise language/original-translation cue to rows. Consider a language filter after confirming the intended catalogue workflow.

Reproduction and source

Content → Records; compare the English rows followed by German rows.

Live screenshot and DOM inspection

P3 UX-28 · Recommendation · Content / record text fields

Long body copy is confined to a four-row editor

The long body field is 90 px tall with 286 px of scrollable content in the sampled English record. It has the same initial row count as the short body.

Why it matters Reviewing a complete article requires a small nested scrolling area; long and short fields have weak visual differentiation.

Suggested correction Give long-form text a larger initial area or an expand-editor action, while keeping short copy compact.

Reproduction and source

Open the tent record and compare Body text (long) with Body text (short).
